## 2

I understand why some space images might seem hard to trust—images can be edited, and institutions can make mistakes. But the evidence that Earth is round doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, see different stars from different parts of Earth, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and track satellites and flights using independent observations. People and organizations around the world, including competing governments and private companies, all make measurements consistent with a spherical Earth. It’s reasonable to question evidence, but the flat-Earth explanation would require all of these separate observations to be faked or misunderstood.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of gas. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some of it is absorbed high in the atmosphere. That’s why the daytime sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue and leaves more red and orange light for us to see.

雨下了一整夜，城市像被一层灰蓝色的薄纱包住。路灯映在积水里，随着雨点落下，碎成一圈圈晃动的金色。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎卷起白亮的水花，很快又消失在巷口。窗玻璃上蜿蜒着细小的水痕，屋里只亮着一盏昏黄的灯。雨声密密地敲着屋檐，像有人在黑暗中低声诉说，整座城市因此显得安静而温柔。
